title: Couchbase: Add support for snapshot marker timestamp
description: The DCP snapshot marker may contain a timestamp

notes.body:
Is this length either 36 or 44, or are other lengths valid?

If this can be other lengths then the "unknown" bytes should be shown somehow.

So it may actually be 0, 36 or 44 (as of today)... In the old days we encoded the packet differently and put everything in the extras section which was decoded earlier (so we would get 0 here). Then at one time we changed the extras section to contain a version field; and then the size should be 36.. then I bumped the version and added the timestamp field so now it is possible to be 44 (not widely used today). In the future it could also be extended with more information..

The code needs some refactor as the extra section wasn't passed down to this function so I couldn't really validate that the version and error out.. For now I just did the simple thing and _added_ the timestamp if it was present.

After pushing the code I also figured that I could be nice and print the timestamp in a "human readable form" (ISO8601) so I got a patch doing that... 

I'll take another stab at how to dump the unknown bytes.

Couchbase: Add support for snapshot marker v2.1

Version 2.1 of DCP Snapshot Marker added an 8 byte timestamp
in network byte order.
